validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE, all resolved. The sheet's current [ref] for Status, Fuel, PipelineType, Capacity, and Location is https://egyptoil-gas.com/?s=Gas+Pipelines+Egypt - a live search-results page (200) that does NOT name 'Damanhur' or 'Tanta' anywhere (confirmed by direct verifier run with those tokens: FAIL). The worklist's own existing_ref_checks already flagged this for Status and Capacity ('200 but data value not found'). Per the scope's existence rule, a citation this generic is itself a red flag - so I searched from scratch rather than accept it.

Found genuine, specific, independent confirmation: (1) Egypt Oil & Gas magazine's dedicated infrastructure report 'A Guide to the Nile Delta's Oil and Gas Resources' (Feb 2020, Issue 158, egyptoil-gas.com/reports/a-guide-to-the-nile-deltas-oil-and-gas-resources/) contains a literal table 'NATURAL GAS INFRASTRUCTURE IN THE NILE DELTA' with columns Pipeline/From/To/Length(Km)/Diameter(Inches). The row reads exactly: 'Damanhur-Tanta | Damanhur | Tanta | 60 | 28' - matching GEM's Length=60.00 km and Diameter=28 in exactly, and confirming direction Damanhur->Tanta. IMPORTANT TEST NOTE: this is a large PDF and url_verifier's automated substring check FAILS on 'Damanhur' and 'Tanta' as standalone tokens (a documented false-negative class per the verifier's own docstring: 'LARGE PDFs - the extractor does not reach the whole document'). I did not accept that FAIL as evidence of absence - I downloaded the PDF directly and ran `pdftotext`, which recovered the full text including the table (lines 549-557 of the extracted text), so the value is genuinely present; I'm citing the URL (it verifies OK on the token 'Nile Delta', which the extractor does reach) with this manual-confirmation caveat documented. The same table also lists Talkha-Tanta-Cairo (125km/28in, matches roster P8024 exactly), Meadia-Damanhur (50km/20in, matches roster P8077 exactly), and Alexandria Network-Damanhur (45km/24in, matches roster P8078 exactly) as three SEPARATE line items with different lengths/diameters from Damanhur-Tanta - this is direct, source-based evidence that P8019 is NOT a duplicate or mislabeling of any of those three superficially similar 'Damanhur'/'Tanta'-adjacent rows; all four are named as distinct physical pipelines in the same primary table.
(2) A second egyptoil-gas.com piece, the feature 'Egypt's Gas Distribution Network, An Intricate Economic Web' (egyptoil-gas.com/features/egypts-gas-distribution-network-an-intricate-economic-web/), states verbatim: 'These pipelines include Abu Madi-Talkha I & II, Talkha-Tanta-Cairo, Abu Madi-Damietta, Meadia-Damanhur, Alexandria Network-Damanhur, Damanhur-Tanta, Cairo Ring-Port Said Line, Korimat-Al Tebbin, and Korimat-Beni Suef. The Damanhur-Tanta line has the largest natural capacity with 700.1 mmcf/d.' This exactly matches GEM's Capacity=700.10 MMcf/d and again lists Damanhur-Tanta as one line among several distinctly-named ones (again arguing against any duplicate reading). Verifier: OK on tokens 'Damanhur-Tanta' + '700.1'.
CLASSIFICATION: 'transmission' is consistent with both sources - this is one of GASCO's named Nile-Delta-area natural gas transmission lines, not a gathering/process/feeder line.
TIER CALL: both supporting documents are published by the same outlet (Egypt Oil & Gas / egyptoil-gas.com), so despite being two separate editorial works (a data-table report vs. a distribution-network feature) with different original numbers, I am NOT treating them as two independent origins per the corroboration rule (same publisher, likely both drawing on GASCO's own published network data). Tier = medium, independent = false. I could not find a second, differently-sourced document giving line-specific length/diameter/capacity figures within this pass; a GASCO/EGAS primary map or table (e.g. the EGAS Annual Report 2018 grid map referenced for other rows in this scope) would be the natural second source but I could not locate/read a usable copy of it before this session's web-search budget was exhausted (200/200 WebSearch calls used) - a separately-sourced spec confirmation stays a genuine open item, not something I'm claiming as done.
Also confirmed via Wikipedia (citable per 2026-08-27 policy) that Damanhur is the seat of Beheira Governorate and Tanta is the seat of Gharbia Governorate, supporting a Location fill below.
